entries.name: mcp__computer-use__computer_batch
entries.description: Execute a sequence of actions in ONE tool call. Each individual tool call requires a model→API round trip (seconds); batching a predictable sequence eliminates all but one. Use this whenever you can predict the outcome of several actions ahead — e.g. click a field, type into it, press Return. Actions execute sequentially and stop on the first error. The frontmost application must be in the session allowlist at the time of this call, or this tool returns an error and does nothing. The frontmost check runs before EACH action inside the batch — if an action opens a non-allowed app, the next action's gate fires and the batch stops there. Screenshot and zoom actions are allowed and their images are returned interleaved with the per-action outputs. Coordinates you write in THIS batch — clicks AND zoom regions — always refer to the full-screen screenshot taken BEFORE this call, never to a zoom and never to a mid-batch screenshot. After the batch returns, the most recent full screenshot it produced becomes the new coordinate reference for your next call. In this session the tools that each carry out one of this tool's actions (left_click, type, key, scroll, left_click_drag, screenshot, etc.) are not available on their own: a single action is a one-item batch. The app_* tools (app_screenshot, app_click, app_type, app_key, app_batch, etc.) act on granted applications without taking over the screen.

action.description: The action to perform.

coordinate.description: (x, y) for click/mouse_move/scroll/left_click_drag end point.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): Rectangle to zoom into. For zoom only. Coordinate space: the full-screen screenshot taken BEFORE this batch (never a mid-batch screenshot, never a prior zoom).

scale.description: For screenshot/zoom only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y) drag start — left_click_drag only. Omit to drag from current cursor.

text.description: For type: the text. For key/hold_key: the chord string. For click/scroll: modifier keys to hold.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every action except mouse_move, scroll, screenshot, zoom, cursor_position and wait. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

actions.description: List of actions. Example: [{"action":"left_click","coordinate":[100,200]},{"action":"type","text":"hello"},{"action":"key","text":"Return"},{"action":"screenshot"},{"action":"zoom","region":[100,100,400,300]}]

save_to_disk.description: Save the images produced by any screenshot/zoom actions in this batch to disk so they can be attached to a message for the user. The saved path(s) are returned in the result. Only set this when you intend to share the image(s) — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__teach_batch
entries.description: Queue multiple teach steps in one tool call. Parallels computer_batch: N steps → one model↔API round trip instead of N. Each step still shows a tooltip and waits for the user's Next click, but YOU aren't waiting for a round trip between steps. You can call teach_batch multiple times in one tour — treat each batch as one predictable SEGMENT (typically: all the steps on one page). The returned screenshot shows the state after the batch's final actions; anchor the NEXT teach_batch against it. WITHIN a batch, all anchors and click coordinates refer to the PRE-BATCH screenshot (same invariant as computer_batch) — for steps 2+ in a batch, either omit anchor (centered tooltip) or target elements you know won't have moved. Good pattern: batch 5 tooltips on page A (last step navigates) → read returned screenshot → batch 3 tooltips on page B → done. Returns {exited:true, stepsCompleted:N} if the user clicks Exit — do NOT call again after that; {stepsCompleted, stepFailed, ...} if an action errors mid-batch; otherwise {stepsCompleted, results:[...]} plus a final screenshot. ---
name: drive-app-with-posted-key-events
description: "Drive the built JusPrin app headlessly (even with the screen locked) by posting CGEvents to its pid with a tiny Swift tool; keys work, mouse clicks do not, and the send dialog is reachable by keyboard."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6b96dccc-1cb4-4f72-9de4-3ecee4b28e74
  modified: 2026-09-08T05:58:16.222Z
---

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). Mouse events posted the same way did nothing, even with the window number set on the event.

Inside `PrintHostSendDialog` (Orca `MsgDialog`), focus starts in the filename field; Tab (48) moves to the "Upload" button, Right (124) to "Upload and Print", Space (49) presses it, because Orca's custom `Button` handles Space/Return and arrow navigation itself. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. Watch the app's own `--datadir` `log/debug_*.log` for effects (use `/usr/bin/grep -a`; the default `grep` is ugrep, which treats `\|` literally and may skip the log as binary). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]].

content.text: The Yes button takes keyboard focus when the dialog opens, so posting a Space key event to this app's pid should press it without full-screen control.

input.command:
R=/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-priceless-gagarin-f193a2/fafd3f95-d2b6-404e-9f74-0cf8294b9c90/scratchpad; mkdir -p $R/tools && cat > $R/tools/postkey.swift <<'EOF'
import CoreGraphics
import Foundation
let a = CommandLine.arguments
let pid = pid_t(a[1])!
for k in a.dropFirst(2) {
    let code = CGKeyCode(k)!
    CGEvent(keyboardEventSource: nil, virtualKey: code, keyDown: true)!.postToPid(pid)
    usleep(50000)
    CGEvent(keyboardEventSource: nil, virtualKey: code, keyDown: false)!.postToPid(pid)
    usleep(200000)
}
EOF
cd $R/tools && swiftc -O postkey.swift -o postkey 2>&1 | tail -2; P=$(pgrep -f "repro/app/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS"); echo pid $P; ./postkey $P 49

# Launch dialogs: options

Untracked working note, 2026-10-28, `jusprin-newui` at a684aee37d. Do not commit.

## What happens

When JusPrin starts, it reopens the most recent project behind Home. If that project was saved for a P1S and a Bambu A1 mini is connected, two OrcaSlicer dialogs block Home before the person has touched anything:

1. **"Tips"**: "Connected printer is Bambu Lab A1 mini… Do you want to sync the printer information and automatically switch the preset?"
2. After Yes, **"Transfer or discard changes"** for "Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle". It lists two settings whose old and new values look the same: G-code thumbnails `48x48/PNG,300x300/…` against `48x48/PNG, 300x300/…` (one space), and Maximum Junction `0.01` against `0.01`. Save writes a modified printer preset.

I reproduced both in a scratch copy of the a684aee37d build with the fake A1 mini. To reach dialog 2 without a click, I stored OrcaSlicer's own "Don't show again + Yes" answer (`sync_after_load_file_show_flag=true`). Screenshots: `frame0-tips-at-launch.jpg` and `frame1-unsaved-changes.jpg` in this session's scratchpad `repro/` folder.

## Where they come from

- **The sync question is OrcaSlicer's.** The block is `Plater::priv::load_files`, `src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:6878-6911`. It runs on any load that carries settings, when a connected Bambu printer differs from the selected printer preset. `git blame` gives 7 commits, and all are in `upstream/*` (BambuStudio 2022 to 2026-05). No fork line is in it.
- **The second dialog is also OrcaSlicer's.** Yes calls `Tab::select_preset`, and that calls `Tab::may_discard_current_dirty_preset` (`Tab.cpp:6278`, upstream). That opens `UnsavedChangesDialog`. No fork commit touches either file. The project's P1S settings differ from the system P1S only in how values are written, but that is enough to count as "changed".
- **The fork seam involved is `answer_modal`** in `DPIAware::ShowModal` (`GUI_Utils.hpp`, fork commits d5bf88a2e4 and 832bb47c31, in no upstream branch). Every OrcaSlicer dialog opens through it, so fork code can answer any dialog without changing OrcaSlicer.

### Why opening from Home showed nothing (frame 1C-01)

- **Open from Home.** `Plater::load_files(wxArrayString)` opens a `FileOpenScope` (fork seam, `Plater.cpp:14216`). `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::file_open_started` then answers every dialog with the least change. For Tips that is No. The answer is recorded and reaches the agent as part of the file report. So the project stays on P1S, nothing is shown, and the agent is told.
- **Launch.** `ProjectAutosave::resume_latest` loads with `LoadStrategy::Restore` (`bbs_3mf.hpp:174`). That strategy includes `Silence`, and `file_load_started` (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:656`) deliberately skips silent loads. It does so for crash recovery and code-internal loads, so their dialogs show "as they always have". Because the resume is not wrapped in any scope, OrcaSlicer asks the person.

Two more facts matter for the options:

- **The launch question depends on timing.** It appears only if the printer has reported in before the resume loads. Here the fake connected 0.6 s before the load. With a slower real printer it may not appear at all. That last part is my expectation, not tested.
- **A stored answer skips every dialog listener.** If someone once ticks "Don't show again", the stored answer applies on every launch and every open: Yes switches the printer silently, No never switches. None of the options below changes that unless it also handles the flag.

## Options

### A. Answer it at launch the way an open does

The resume load gets the same least-change answers as an open from Home. In `resume_latest`, the fork-owned `ProjectAutosave.cpp`, put a `ScopedLeastChangeAnswers` around `load_managed_checkpoint` and record what was answered.

- **What the person sees.** Home appears with no dialog. The project stays on its P1S preset, exactly as after an open from Home. Nothing tells them about the mismatch until they try to print to the A1 mini.
- **OrcaSlicer-owned lines touched:** none. **Rebase cost:** none.
- **Cost:** under an hour, plus a check in the real app.

### B. A, plus the mismatch shown as a fact on the header printer chip

Do A. Then, in Prepare, the printer chip notes that the connected printer is not the one the project is set up for (for example "Set up for P1S · A1 mini connected"). Its menu offers to switch. Fork-owned code compares the selected preset's printer model with the connected machine on every refresh. That covers launch, Home opens, agent opens and printers connecting later, all through one path.

- **What the person sees.** The same behaviour at launch and on open: no modal, and a visible fact where the printer is shown. The 2026-10-26 setup-card decision sends printer-model mismatches to the header chip. However, `PrinterFilamentChip.hpp` currently says the chip "never warns". This would be a fact, but the wording needs your call.
- **Catch.** Switching from the chip goes through `Tab::select_preset` (`SetupCommands::select_printer_preset`). That would raise the same "Transfer or discard changes" dialog with the two non-changes. It needs a fork-side answer, such as Discard for formatting-only differences, or carrying settings over the way `release_project` drops edited presets.
- **OrcaSlicer-owned lines touched:** none. **Rebase cost:** none.
- **Cost:** a day or two, mostly in the chip, the menu row, and the switch.

### C. A, plus the agent handles the mismatch

Do A. Then put the mismatch into the project state the agent reads, so the agent raises it and offers `printer_change`.

- **What the person sees.** No modal. The mismatch comes up only when the agent speaks. A resumed project has no new agent turn, and a person without an agent set up hears nothing at all.
- **OrcaSlicer-owned lines touched:** none. **Rebase cost:** none.
- **Cost:** prompt work plus evals, which need your approval to spend on live-model runs.

**Rejected: skipping the block for `Restore` loads inside `Plater.cpp`.** It does the same job as A, but it rewrites an upstream condition that upstream is still editing (2026-05). That is fork-stewardship principle 3.

## How this lines up with "a 3MF for another printer switches the printer silently"

Both tasks are one fact seen twice. Opening the P1S file replaces the person's A1 mini with the file's P1S preset (the log shows `A1 mini 2` → `P1S 0.4 nozzle` during the resume), and OrcaSlicer then asks to switch back.

Decide once what a project is on after opening a file made for another printer:

- **If the sibling task keeps the person's printer on open,** this question never arises for the connected printer. A becomes a safety net.
- **If it keeps the file's printer,** B's chip fact is that task's visible signal too.

Either way, both should share one comparison: the project's printer against the person's printer.

## Recommendation

**B**, built in two steps. A first: it is small, has no rebase cost, removes the blocking dialogs today, and makes launch match open. Then the chip fact, designed together with the sibling task so one comparison drives both.

Decide on the chip wording, and on the stored-answer flag (ignore it, or clear it), when you choose.

Untracked working note, 2026-10-28, `jusprin-newui` at a684aee37d. Do not commit.

## What happens

When JusPrin starts, it reopens the most recent project behind Home. If that project was saved for a P1S and a Bambu A1 mini is connected, two OrcaSlicer dialogs block Home before the person has touched anything:

1. **"Tips"**: "Connected printer is Bambu Lab A1 mini… Do you want to sync the printer information and automatically switch the preset?"
2. After Yes, **"Transfer or discard changes"** for "Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle". It lists two settings whose old and new values look the same: G-code thumbnails `48x48/PNG,300x300/…` against `48x48/PNG, 300x300/…` (one space), and Maximum Junction `0.01` against `0.01`. Save writes a modified printer preset.

I reproduced both in a scratch copy of the a684aee37d build with the fake A1 mini. To reach dialog 2 without a click, I stored OrcaSlicer's own "Don't show again + Yes" answer (`sync_after_load_file_show_flag=true`). Screenshots: `frame0-tips-at-launch.jpg` and `frame1-unsaved-changes.jpg` in this session's scratchpad `repro/` folder.

## Where they come from

- **The sync question is OrcaSlicer's.** The block is `Plater::priv::load_files`, `src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:6878-6911`. It runs on any load that carries settings, when a connected Bambu printer differs from the selected printer preset. `git blame` gives 7 commits, and all are in `upstream/*` (BambuStudio 2022 to 2026-05). No fork line is in it.
- **The second dialog is also OrcaSlicer's.** Yes calls `Tab::select_preset`, and that calls `Tab::may_discard_current_dirty_preset` (`Tab.cpp:6278`, upstream). That opens `UnsavedChangesDialog`. No fork commit touches either file. The project's P1S settings differ from the system P1S only in how values are written, but that is enough to count as "changed".
- **The fork seam involved is `answer_modal`** in `DPIAware::ShowModal` (`GUI_Utils.hpp`, fork commits d5bf88a2e4 and 832bb47c31, in no upstream branch). Every OrcaSlicer dialog opens through it, so fork code can answer any dialog without changing OrcaSlicer.

### Why opening from Home showed nothing (frame 1C-01)

- **Open from Home.** `Plater::load_files(wxArrayString)` opens a `FileOpenScope` (fork seam, `Plater.cpp:14216`). `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::file_open_started` then answers every dialog with the least change. For Tips that is No. The answer is recorded and reaches the agent as part of the file report. So the project stays on P1S, nothing is shown, and the agent is told.
- **Launch.** `ProjectAutosave::resume_latest` loads with `LoadStrategy::Restore` (`bbs_3mf.hpp:174`). That strategy includes `Silence`, and `file_load_started` (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:656`) deliberately skips silent loads. It does so for crash recovery and code-internal loads, so their dialogs show "as they always have". Because the resume is not wrapped in any scope, OrcaSlicer asks the person.

Two more facts matter for the options:

- **The launch question depends on timing.** It appears only if the printer has reported in before the resume loads. Here the fake connected 0.6 s before the load. With a slower real printer it may not appear at all. That last part is my expectation, not tested.
- **A stored answer skips every dialog listener.** If someone once ticks "Don't show again", the stored answer applies on every launch and every open: Yes switches the printer silently, No never switches. None of the options below changes that unless it also handles the flag.

## Options

### A. Answer it at launch the way an open does

The resume load gets the same least-change answers as an open from Home. In `resume_latest`, the fork-owned `ProjectAutosave.cpp`, put a `ScopedLeastChangeAnswers` around `load_managed_checkpoint` and record what was answered.

- **What the person sees.** Home appears with no dialog. The project stays on its P1S preset, exactly as after an open from Home. Nothing tells them about the mismatch until they try to print to the A1 mini.
- **OrcaSlicer-owned lines touched:** none. **Rebase cost:** none.
- **Cost:** under an hour, plus a check in the real app.

### B. A, plus the mismatch shown as a fact on the header printer chip

Do A. Then, in Prepare, the printer chip notes that the connected printer is not the one the project is set up for (for example "Set up for P1S · A1 mini connected"). Its menu offers to switch. Fork-owned code compares the selected preset's printer model with the connected machine on every refresh. That covers launch, Home opens, agent opens and printers connecting later, all through one path.

- **What the person sees.** The same behaviour at launch and on open: no modal, and a visible fact where the printer is shown. The 2026-10-26 setup-card decision sends printer-model mismatches to the header chip. However, `PrinterFilamentChip.hpp` currently says the chip "never warns". This would be a fact, but the wording needs your call.
- **Catch.** Switching from the chip goes through `Tab::select_preset` (`SetupCommands::select_printer_preset`). That would raise the same "Transfer or discard changes" dialog with the two non-changes. It needs a fork-side answer, such as Discard for formatting-only differences, or carrying settings over the way `release_project` drops edited presets.
- **OrcaSlicer-owned lines touched:** none. **Rebase cost:** none.
- **Cost:** a day or two, mostly in the chip, the menu row, and the switch.

### C. A, plus the agent handles the mismatch

Do A. Then put the mismatch into the project state the agent reads, so the agent raises it and offers `printer_change`.

- **What the person sees.** No modal. The mismatch comes up only when the agent speaks. A resumed project has no new agent turn, and a person without an agent set up hears nothing at all.
- **OrcaSlicer-owned lines touched:** none. **Rebase cost:** none.
- **Cost:** prompt work plus evals, which need your approval to spend on live-model runs.

**Rejected: skipping the block for `Restore` loads inside `Plater.cpp`.** It does the same job as A, but it rewrites an upstream condition that upstream is still editing (2026-05). That is fork-stewardship principle 3.

## How this lines up with "a 3MF for another printer switches the printer silently"

Both tasks are one fact seen twice. Opening the P1S file replaces the person's A1 mini with the file's P1S preset (the log shows `A1 mini 2` → `P1S 0.4 nozzle` during the resume), and OrcaSlicer then asks to switch back.

Decide once what a project is on after opening a file made for another printer:

- **If the sibling task keeps the person's printer on open,** this question never arises for the connected printer. A becomes a safety net.
- **If it keeps the file's printer,** B's chip fact is that task's visible signal too.

Either way, both should share one comparison: the project's printer against the person's printer.

## Recommendation

**B**, built in two steps. A first: it is small, has no rebase cost, removes the blocking dialogs today, and makes launch match open. Then the chip fact, designed together with the sibling task so one comparison drives both.

Decide on the chip wording, and on the stored-answer flag (ignore it, or clear it), when you choose.

I reproduced both launch dialogs in a scratch copy of the a684aee37d build. The options note is in [launch-dialogs-options.md](launch-dialogs-options.md), untracked; I changed no code and committed nothing. My recommendation is option B, built in two steps: option A first, then a note on the header chip. Nothing gets implemented until you choose.

**What I found**
- **Both dialogs are OrcaSlicer's own code.** The sync question is in [Plater.cpp:6878](src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:6878). All 7 commits behind it come from upstream (`git blame` checked against the `upstream/*` branches). "Transfer or discard changes" is the dialog OrcaSlicer shows when you switch away from a printer preset it thinks was edited.
- **The two "changed" settings aren't real changes.** The thumbnail list differs by one space, and Maximum Junction shows 0.01 on both sides.
- **Why launch asks but opening from Home doesn't:**
  - **Opening from Home:** JusPrin's `FileOpenScope` (a fork addition) answers every OrcaSlicer dialog with the choice that changes least. For this question that is No, and the agent is told about it. That is why frame 1C-01 showed nothing.
  - **Launch:** reopening the last project loads it as a silent load. `file_load_started` ([OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:657](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:657)) deliberately leaves silent loads alone, so OrcaSlicer asks the person directly.
- **The launch question depends on timing.** It only appears if the printer has connected before the project finishes loading. Here the fake printer connected 0.6 s earlier. With a slower real printer it may not appear at all; that is my expectation, not tested.
- **A stored "Don't show again" answer skips all of this.** Once someone ticks it, launches and opens switch the printer silently (if they chose Yes) or never switch (if No).

**The options** (none changes an OrcaSlicer-owned line):
- **A:** at launch, answer the question the same way an open from Home does. No dialog appears and the project stays on P1S. About an hour of work in the fork-owned `ProjectAutosave.cpp`.
- **B:** A, plus a note on the header printer chip in Prepare, such as "Set up for P1S · A1 mini connected", with an option to switch. This gives the same behaviour at launch and on open. The catch: switching from the chip still raises the same "Transfer or discard changes" dialog over the two non-changes, so that needs handling in fork code too.
- **C:** A, plus the agent raises the mismatch. But a reopened project gets no new agent message, and someone without an agent set up would hear nothing.

**Link to the "switches the printer silently" task:** it's the same mismatch. Opening the P1S file replaces the A1 mini with the file's printer, and OrcaSlicer then offers to switch back. Decide once which printer a project uses after opening a file made for another printer. If the other task keeps your printer, this question never comes up and A is just a safety net. If it keeps the file's printer, B's chip note becomes that task's visible signal too.

**Two calls are yours if you pick B:**
- **Chip wording:** `PrinterFilamentChip.hpp` says the chip "never warns", while your 2026-10-26 setup-card decision moves printer mismatches to the header chip.
- **The stored "Don't show again" answer:** whether to ignore it or clear it.

Screenshots of both dialogs are in `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-priceless-gagarin-f193a2/fafd3f95-d2b6-404e-9f74-0cf8294b9c90/scratchpad/repro/`. I couldn't press Yes in the real dialog: a background click was refused because another app's window covered that spot. So I reached the second dialog by storing OrcaSlicer's own "Don't show again + Yes" answer in the scratch config, which runs the same switch without asking.

This session's branch now points at `jusprin-newui` (a684aee37d), because the worktree had started on an old commit without the JusPrin code.

description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

+    // A project made elsewhere can name a filament preset this app does not

+    // of the project must not ask again.
+        // Not checked: the adapter torn down earlier in this run took the

+    //
+    // Orca does not reload a project preset with no parent preset. It rebuilds
+    // it from the project's settings and names it after the file, which for a

+        // Every reload keeps the name the person saw. Orca rebuilds a preset
+        // with no parent from the project's settings and names it after the
+        // file it came from, which for a checkpoint added "(.3mf)".
+        // The restore saved a version holding the name it reloaded, so
+        // restoring that version again would add to it.
Skip Orca's 3MF preset check when reloading a checkpoint

Reloading a project checkpoint (launch resume, opening a project from
Home, revert) could show Orca's "Customized Preset" or "Modified G-code"
dialog. A checkpoint is JusPrin's own copy of a project that Orca
already checked when the person first opened it, so the reload should
look like nothing happened.

Plater.cpp: the preset safety check after a 3MF load now also skips
LoadStrategy::Restore loads. This also stops Orca's crash-backup restore,
which uses Restore, from warning a second time.

ProjectAutosave.cpp: remove the listener from e3f826a83c that answered
any dialog titled "Modified G-code" during a checkpoint reload. The
condition in Plater.cpp makes it unnecessary.

Rebase note: upstream ee6d195b0e changes the same line to
`if (!published_config.published && (choise.empty() || ...))`. Keep both
conditions when resolving.

Tested with the workspace harness (tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness):
a new check, verify_unknown_preset_checkpoint, opens a 3MF whose filament
preset is not installed and has no parent, then restores an earlier
checkpoint and fails if any Orca dialog appears. Before the change it
showed "Customized Preset"; with the old listener removed, the existing
restore check also showed "Modified G-code". Both pass now.

Keep a project-only preset's name when reloading a checkpoint

Reloading a checkpoint renamed a project-only preset that has no parent

came back as "...(unknown-preset.3mf)(.3mf)". Restore saves a new version
straight away, so the name grew by one "(.3mf)" on every restore and every
open from Home.

Cause: each checkpoint load first clears the project-only presets. Orca
then skips reloading a stored preset with no parent ("don't load project
embedded preset when can not find inherit"), and load_external_preset

3
[Opening and importing files](architecture.md#opening-and-importing-files).
The project document has one schema version and no migration (the project is
not live yet): a document of any other version, like a corrupt one, is
replaced by a fresh document. The local store reads only its current index,
manifest and current-document formats.
Recent projects appear on Home and in the header menu. Selecting one
opens its managed version even when its imported source file has been removed.
The most recently authored local project resumes on startup.

## Chosen defaults and limits

- The controller checks a lightweight native state signature every 2 seconds
  and waits 1.5 seconds after an observed model edit before starting a background
  model save. Document changes use the coalesced state write described above;
  they never call Orca's 3MF exporter. An unchanged project does not run the
  exporter. Project replacement and Agent boundaries save synchronously.
| Dropped on Home | Same | Same |
| Home's **Open…** button, File › Open Project (Cmd+O) | Same | Same |
| Dropped on the Prepare canvas | Added to the open project | New project, as above. OrcaSlicer's "open as project or import geometry?" question is not asked |
| **+ Add model** in the Plates and Project pane, File › Import (Cmd+I) | Added to the open project | Its geometry is added to the open project, without its settings (OrcaSlicer's Import) |
| The Agent composer's + › 3D model, a drop on the Agent pane, or a request in the chat | Attached; the agent adds it to the open project (`object_import`) | Same |

Rules that follow from the table:

- A model file never silently lands in whatever project happened to be open behind Home. Before 2026-10-24 Home's Import button did exactly that, because it called OrcaSlicer's `add_model`, and from 2026-09-30 a project was always open behind Home (the most recent one resumes at startup).
- A file opened from the OS lands in the running JusPrin. OrcaSlicer's default starts a second process for a .3mf; JusPrin runs as a single instance on every platform.
- Several files opened or dropped together make one new project holding all of them.
- Opening a .3mf as a project is the only thing a .3mf does on the Prepare canvas. Wanting only the geometry out of a .3mf is rare, and the agent or File › Import can do it on request. The one question JusPrin asks on a file open stays the "Previously opened file" question described in the [autosave document](autosave-version-history.md).
- Home's primary action is **Open…**, not Import: there is nothing on Home to import into. The whole Home page accepts a dropped file, and its empty state says so ("Drop a model or project here, or Open…"). Beside it, **New** is the design system's compact outlined button (`secondarySmall`, 28 DIP) for a blank project built up part by part, quiet enough not to compete with Open; File › New Project does the same.

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers
REQUIRE_THAT(value, WithinRel(expected, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));
```

### Sections for Test Organization
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Complex feature testing", "[Feature]") {
    // Common setup code
    SomeObject obj;
    
    SECTION("First scenario") {
        // Specific test case
        REQUIRE(obj.method1() == expected_value);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second scenario") {
        // Another test case with same setup
        REQUIRE(obj.method2() == other_expected);
    }
}
```

### BDD-Style Tests
Use for complex scenarios and user story testing:

> **Note**: BDD macros are aliases for TEST_CASE and SECTION with prefixed names
```cpp
SCENARIO("User performs complex operation", "[UserStory]") {
    GIVEN("A specific setup condition") {
        GCodeWriter writer;
        // Setup code
        
        WHEN("User performs action") {
            auto result = writer.some_operation();
            
            THEN("Expected outcome occurs") {
                REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
                
                AND_WHEN("Follow-up action occurs") {
                    auto next_result = writer.next_operation();
                    
                    THEN("Final outcome is correct") {
                        REQUIRE(next_result == expected);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Data Generators for Parameterized Tests
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Function works with various inputs", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto test_value = GENERATE(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13);
    
    REQUIRE(is_odd(test_value));
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Range-based generators
TEST_CASE("Range testing", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto i = GENERATE(range(1, 10));  // 1 to 9
    REQUIRE(process_value(i) > i);
}

// Using variables in generators (requires GENERATE_COPY or GENERATE_REF)
TEST_CASE("Generator with variables", "[Algorithm]") {
    std::vector<int> values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    auto test_value = GENERATE_REF(from_range(values));  // Use GENERATE_REF for references
    
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Custom generators
TEST_CASE("Random values", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto random_int = GENERATE(take(100, random(-1000, 1000)));  // 100 random values
    REQUIRE(process_random_value(random_int));
}
```

### Test Fixtures
```cpp
class GeometryFixture {
public:
    Point origin{0, 0};
    Point unit_x{1, 0};
    Point unit_y{0, 1};
    
    mutable double tolerance = EPSILON;  // Use mutable for data that might change
};

// Standard fixture - new instance per test run
TEST_CASE_METHOD(GeometryFixture, "Point operations", "[Geometry]") {
    REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
}

// Persistent fixture - single instance for entire test case (v3.2.0+)
TEST_CASE_PERSISTENT_FIXTURE(GeometryFixture, "Persistent operations", "[Geometry]") {
    static int call_count = 0;
    ++call_count;
    INFO("This fixture persists across sections, call: " << call_count);
    
    SECTION("First section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_y) == 1.0);
        // call_count will be 2 here with persistent fixture
    }
}

// Template fixtures for type-parameterized tests
template<typename T>
class NumericFixture {
public:
    T zero = T{0};
    T one = T{1};
};

TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE_METHOD(NumericFixture, "Numeric operations", "[Template]", int, float, double) {
    REQUIRE(TestType{} == this->zero);
    REQUIRE(TestType{1} == this->one);
}
```

### Advanced Testing Features

#### Logging and Information Macros
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Advanced logging", "[Logging]") {
    INFO("This info persists until end of scope");
    
    SECTION("Section A") {
        INFO("Section A specific info");
        CAPTURE(some_variable, another_var);  // Captures variable names and values
        CHECK(some_condition);
    }
    
    SECTION("Section B") {
        UNSCOPED_INFO("This survives beyond its scope");  // v2.7.0+
        CHECK(other_condition);
    }
}

// Warning and explicit control
TEST_CASE("Explicit test control", "[Control]") {
    WARN("This warns but doesn't fail the test");
    
    if (precondition_not_met) {
        SKIP("Reason");  // Marks the test as skipped (v3.3.0+, available)
        return;
    }
    
    if (critical_failure) {
        FAIL("Critical condition failed");  // Fails and stops test
    }
    
    SUCCEED("Reached successful completion");  // Explicit success marker
}
```

#### Static Assertions (Compile-time Testing)
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Compile-time checks", "[Static]") {
    STATIC_REQUIRE(sizeof(int) >= 4);  // Checked at compile time
    STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(std::is_void_v<int>);
    
    // For traits and template metaprogramming
    STATIC_CHECK(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<Point>);  // v3.0.1+
}
```

#### Conditional Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Conditional blocks", "[Conditional]") {
    int value = get_test_value();
    
    // These record the expression but don't count as test failures (v3.0.1+)
    CHECKED_IF(value > 0) {
        // This block runs if value > 0
        REQUIRE(value <= 100);
    } CHECKED_ELSE(value > 0) {
        // This block runs if value <= 0  
        REQUIRE(value >= -100);
    }
}
```

#### Benchmarking (v2.9.0+)
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance testing", "[Benchmark]") {
    // Simple benchmarking
    BENCHMARK("Algorithm performance") {
        return expensive_algorithm();
    };
    
    // Advanced benchmarking with setup
    BENCHMARK_ADVANCED("Advanced benchmark")(Catch::Benchmark::Chronometer meter) {
        std::vector<int> data = setup_test_data();  // Setup not measured
        
        meter.measure([&] { 
            return process_data(data);  // Only this is measured
        });
    };
}
```

## OrcaSlicer-Specific Testing Patterns

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

```
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
```

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers
REQUIRE_THAT(value, WithinRel(expected, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));
```

### Sections for Test Organization
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Complex feature testing", "[Feature]") {
    // Common setup code
    SomeObject obj;
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)
